paragraphs: Moses pushed back: "They're not gonna trust me. They won't listen to a single word I say. They'll just laugh — 'God appeared to him? Yeah, right!'"
So God asked, "What's that in your hand?" "Just a staff," Moses said.
"Throw it on the ground." Moses threw it down — and it turned into a snake! Moses jumped back so fast!

God told Moses, "Now grab it by the tail." He reached out and grabbed it — and boom, it was his staff again. "That's how they'll know God appeared to you — the God of their ancestors, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob."
Then God said, "Put your hand inside your shirt." Moses slipped his hand under his shirt and pulled it out — and his hand had turned leprous, white as snow.
God said, "Now put your hand back under your shirt." He did — and when he pulled it out, it was totally healthy again.

"So if they don't believe you after the first sign, the second one should convince them. And if they still don't trust you or listen to you after both signs — take some water from the Nile and pour it on dry ground. The moment it hits the dirt, that Nile water will turn into blood."
Moses tried another excuse on God: "Master, please — I'm terrible at speaking. I never was good with words, not before and not now either. I stutter and stammer."

God said, "Who do you think made the human mouth? Who makes people mute or deaf, sighted or blind? Isn't it me, God? So get going! I'll be right there with you — with your mouth! I'll teach you exactly what to say."
Moses said, "Oh, Master, please! Just send someone else!"

God got angry with Moses: "Don't you have a brother — Aaron the Levite? He's great with words, I know he is. He speaks really well. Actually, he's already on his way to meet you right now, and he'll be so happy to see you. You'll tell him what to say. I'll be with both of you as you speak, teaching you step by step. He'll speak to the people for you — he'll be your mouth, but you decide what comes out of it. Now pick up that staff — you're going to do the signs with it."
Moses went back to his father-in-law Jethro and said, "I need to go back to my relatives in Egypt. I want to check if they're still alive." Jethro said, "Go — and peace be with you."
God told Moses while he was still in Midian: "Go back to Egypt. All the men who wanted you dead are dead now."
So Moses put his wife and sons on a donkey and headed back to Egypt, holding tight to the staff of God.

God told Moses, "When you get back to Egypt, get ready: all the wonders I'm going to do through you — you'll perform them right in front of Pharaoh. But I'm going to make him stubborn, so he'll refuse to let the people go. Then tell Pharaoh this message from God: 'Israel is my son, my firstborn! I told you to free my son so he can serve me. You refused. So now I'm going to kill your son — your firstborn.'"

On the way back, while they were camped for the night, God confronted Moses and was about to kill him — but Zipporah grabbed a sharp flint knife, circumcised her son, and touched Moses with the foreskin. She cried out, "You're a bridegroom of blood to me!" Then God let him go. She said "bridegroom of blood" because of the circumcision.

God told Aaron, "Go meet Moses out in the wilderness." Aaron went and met him at the mountain of God, and kissed him. Moses told Aaron everything God had sent him to say and all the wonders God had commanded him to do.

So Moses and Aaron gathered all of Israel's leaders. Aaron told them everything God had told Moses, and performed the wonders right in front of the people. The people believed — they trusted that God had seen what the Israelites were going through and knew all about their suffering. They bowed down low and worshiped.
title: Signs and Excuses
